strings.name: Yann LeCun
strings.role: Deep learning pioneer · Computer vision and world models
strings.summary: Yann LeCun helped bring convolutional networks into applications such as handwriting recognition, developing LeNet and gradient-based methods with collaborators. He built research programs at Bell Labs, NYU and FAIR, and shared the Turing Award with Hinton and Bengio. After leaving Meta, he co-founded AMI to study models of the physical world, an approach still under active development.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026. This is not a daily news record. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced convolutional networks and computer vision, making foundational contributions to deep learning and its large-scale applications.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Convolutional networks and recognition
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Worked with Bottou, Bengio, Haffner and others on networks for documents and handwriting.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Sustained research leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Built academic and industrial machine-learning programs and later expanded his focus to world models.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: AMI announced seed funding
strings.timeline.event-1.text: The company he co-founded raised funds for world-model research; funding does not establish that its goals are achieved.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Left Meta
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Ended his period as Meta’s chief AI scientist and moved toward new research and entrepreneurial arrangements.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: 2018 Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.event-3.text: ACM named LeCun, Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio joint recipients.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Founded Facebook AI Research
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Became FAIR’s founding director, organizing long-term AI research.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joined NYU
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Became a professor researching machine learning, vision and computational perception.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Document recognition research
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Published with collaborators on gradient-based learning and convolutional networks, including LeNet-5.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Joined Bell Labs
strings.timeline.event-7.text: After postdoctoral work in Toronto, joined AT&T Bell Labs to research neural networks.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Computer science doctorate
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Earned a PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University, then moved to Toronto for research.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Engineering diploma
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Graduated from ESIEE Paris with training in electronics and computing.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in France
